bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical disruptions (West Asia) impacting input costs & exports; inflationary pressure on distribution & packaging; delayed Telangana price hike; ESOP charges (₹5-6cr/quarter); brand cannibalization risk between ICONiQ and SRB7/OC Blue
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, forward-looking, disciplined; strong emphasis on premiumization, backward integration, and long-term margin expansion; leadership transition (Amar Sinha) underway with clear 3-year roadmap; cautious on near-term margin pressure but optimistic on H2 recovery
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: OC Brandy in AP (12-13M case market) is a hidden millionaire brand opportunity; ₹27/franchise fee elimination in UP will materially boost OC margins; ABD Maestro’s 3-year path: CM3 negative → CM2 neutral → CM3 neutral (EBITDA breakeven by Year 3); CSD approvals are a structural moat for premium brands
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Stated financial framework caps leverage at Net Debt/EBITDA below 2.0x and Net Debt/Equity below 0.75x through the capex phase; FY26 stood at 1.7x and 0.6x respectively.
- ROCE (pre-tax) trajectory targeted from 18.5% in FY26 to 23%-25% by FY28, with EBITDA margin from 14.4% (FY26) to ~18% and gross margin from 45.6% to ~48%.
- Prudent 'Build | Buy | Partner' allocation framework with capex primarily funded through internal accruals; net IPO proceeds (Jul-24) were used to repay high-cost debt and statutory arrears.
- Operating cash flow has improved consistently from a negative Rs 729 Cr in H1FY25 (Telangana overdues and statutory arrears) to Rs 215 Cr in H2FY26, funding deleveraging alongside the capex program.
- The deck makes no mention of dividends or buybacks; free cash flow is directed to net debt reduction and reinvestment.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Strong leadership position in the Indian whisky segment, anchored by flagship Mass Premium brand Officer's Choice Whisky with deep brand recall and consumer franchise
- Three 'millionaire brand' whiskies in Prestige & Above (Officer's Choice Blue, Sterling Reserve B7, ICONiQ White Whisky) providing scale across large, fast-growing price points
- Extensive pan-India manufacturing network combining owned and third-party (exclusive/non-exclusive) facilities, enabling operational flexibility and proximity to consumption centres
- Extensive distribution reach - 80,000+ retail touchpoints domestically and an asset-light, high-margin export model across 36 countries
- Backward integration into ENA, malt and packaging (PET) enhancing supply security, cost structure and margin resilience
- Diversified super-premium to luxury portfolio via ABD Maestro (80%-held subsidiary), built on a 'Build, Buy & Partner' model spanning whisky, gin, vodka and rum
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Market risk (interest rate, FX, inflation, macro factors) — ABDL is exposed to movements in interest rates, foreign exchange rates, inflation and other macroeconomic factors that may influence input costs, pricing, demand and profitability.
- Interest rate risk — Interest rate movements may affect borrowing costs and returns on surplus funds; managed through prudent treasury practices and an appropriate funding mix.
- Foreign currency risk — Exposure arises from imports of raw materials, packaging components and capital goods, and from export transactions; currency fluctuations can affect costs and realisations.
- Inflation risk on input costs — Inflation in raw materials, packaging, freight and other operating inputs can pressure margins, requiring cost optimisation, sourcing discipline and calibrated pricing actions.
- Credit risk — Arises primarily from trade receivables and placement of surplus funds with banks/financial institutions; managed via credit policies, customer evaluation and expected-credit-loss principles.
- Liquidity risk — Risk of being unable to meet financial obligations as they fall due; managed through cash-flow planning, working-capital review and access to banking lines.
- Regulatory and taxation risk (state excise framework) — The alcoholic beverages industry operates within a complex and evolving state-level regulatory environment covering excise policy, taxation, licensing and route-to-market structures, which can affect pricing, distribution and profitability.
- Cybersecurity and data protection risk — As digital systems become more integral to operations, the Company is exposed to cybersecurity and data-protection risks that could cause operational disruption, data loss and reputational impact.

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- 2nd largest Indian spirits company by volume with 31 brands spanning whisky, brandy, rum, vodka and gin across multiple price points from Rs 840 to Rs 5,300 per 750ml bottle.
- Four Millionaire Brands: Officer's Choice (3rd largest whisky in the world, top 10 global spirits brand, 40%+ share of Mass Premium), ICONiQ White (world's fastest growing millionaire whisky for CY23, CY24 and CY25), Sterling Reserve B7 and Officer's Choice Blue.
- India's largest spirits exporter by volume, present in 39 countries with market leadership in the Middle East and a growing Africa footprint; export model is asset-light with profitability ~1.3x domestic and working capital ~1/3rd of domestic.
- Distribution moat of 80,000+ retail touchpoints covering 90%+ of the width of Indian retail across 30+ states/UTs, with 12 sales support offices and route-to-market expertise across open, corporation, wholesale, defence and export channels.
- Board and senior management stacked with sector veterans from United Spirits, Diageo, Pernod Ricard, Radico Khaitan, LVMH/Moet Hennessy and Glenmorangie, supporting the move up the premium ladder.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition - UP] Announced Jan-26 acquisition of a non-operational distillery cum bottling facility (land, building, plant, machinery and licences) in Moradabad, UP from National Industrial Corporation Private Limited for Rs 70 Cr, to become the 3rd integrated facility.
- [Acquisition - AP] Announced Mar-26 acquisition of up to a 50% stake in Kion Blenders Industries Private Limited (Rs 300 Cr investment, Rs 90 Cr equity split Rs 45 Cr each with the existing shareholder) to set up the 66 MLPA Vizianagaram dual-mode distillery.
- [Regulation] Management flags the UK FTA as margin-enhancing for the premium and luxury portfolio, and describes the state regulatory landscape as supportive with further momentum expected from the Telangana policy and anticipated price revisions.
- [Receivables] Improving sentiment in Telangana for gradual clearance of outstanding dues; historic Telangana overdues and statutory arrears were the driver of the large negative H1FY25 operating cash flow.
- [Management] Amar Sinha joined as Managing Director in 2026 (ex-Radico Khaitan, Whyte & Mackay India), with a Chief Revenue Officer, Group CMO and Chief Procurement Officer also newly appointed or re-designated effective 1 Aug 2026.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Allied Blenders and Distillers Limited manufactures, markets and distributes Indian Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL), with a diversified brand portfolio spanning Mass Premium and Prestige & Above (P&A) price segments across whisky, vodka, rum, gin and brandy. The Company serves state government-owned beverage corporations, the Canteen Stores Department (defence), and private distributors/retailers domestically, reaching consumers through an extensive network of licensed retail outlets, bars, restaurants and hotels, while international markets are served through distributor and partner relationships. ABDL operates an extensive pan-India manufacturing and distribution network combining owned and partner (third-party) facilities, and has been strengthening backward integration into ENA, malt and PET packaging.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Deliver profitable, value-led growth through premiumisation, portfolio diversification, distribution expansion and disciplined execution
- Scale the Prestige & Above (P&A) portfolio and expand the ABD Maestro luxury-spirits business
- Accelerate the international business, leveraging an integrated value chain and strategic backward integration to enhance competitiveness
- Pursue opportunities across Travel Retail, Canteen Stores Department (CSD) and the evolving UK-India FTA framework
- Transformation roadmap centred on premiumisation, backward integration and operational efficiencies, refining the portfolio and tightening supply-chain control to unlock margin strength
- Portfolio build-up via a calibrated 'Build, Buy & Partner' model, combining in-house capabilities with strategic partnerships and acquisitions
- Prestige & Semi-Premium segment: accelerate aggregate market share in India and international markets, and launch new products in available white spaces
- Premium / Super-premium to luxury segment: sharp focus on key markets and high-headroom defence channel, multi-flavour portfolio build, and a new team with new skills for premium on-premise and key-account channels
- Strengthen governance frameworks, compliance processes and enterprise-wide risk management as the organisation scales
- Invest in structured talent development, capability enhancement, digital enablement and leadership-focused initiatives to build a more agile, high-performance organisation
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: ABDL's capex programme is focused on strengthening backward integration, securing critical inputs (ENA, Malt, PET) and expanding manufacturing capabilities, implemented through Phase I and Phase II investments. Phase I (captive integration): (1) a captive PET bottle manufacturing facility at Rangapur, Telangana was commissioned during the year, with ~600+ Mn bottles per annum capacity and ~70-75% internal requirement coverage, and has been EBITDA accretive since Q3 FY26; (2) a single malt distillery at Rangapur, Telangana (~4.0 MLPA capacity) continued under development to secure captive malt for the Prestige & Above portfolio and build Single Malt whisky capability; (3) an ENA capacity expansion at an acquired ~11 MLPA distillery in Aurangabad, Maharashtra (operations commenced February 2025), with a major expansion initiative underway to significantly increase ENA distillation capacity toward a planned 66 MLPA (also referenced as a planned expansion to ~61 MLPA), strengthening backward integration in a key operating market. Phase II (downstream growth), initiated during the year: bottling capacity expansion in Uttar Pradesh (bottling-unit upgradation, ~40 Cr investment) to strengthen manufacturing presence in a key growth market; bottling capacity expansion at the Aurangabad, Maharashtra facility to support western-market and international demand; and an ENA Distillery (Dual Mode) project in Vizianagaram, Andhra Pradesh via an up-to-50% stake acquired in KION Blenders Industries Private Limited. The narrative text also cites additional investment figures of approximately ~260 Cr, ~110 Cr, ~54 Cr and ~300 Cr associated with the ENA/Phase II projects, but the source formatting does not cleanly attribute each figure to a single named project, so they are reported here only as a range of disclosed amounts rather than assigned individually. Collectively, the current projects are expected to enhance EBITDA margins by ~300 bps by FY28 and an incremental ~100 bps by FY29. ABD Maestro (the super-premium to luxury subsidiary) separately has two strategically located manufacturing facilities in the pipeline to enable efficient small-batch premium production.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's real GDP growth projected in the range of 6.8%-7.2% for FY2026-27, supported by resilient consumption, continued government expenditure and an improving private investment cycle
- Rising disposable incomes and evolving consumer preferences expected to continue supporting premiumisation trends across categories
- Indian spirits industry transitioning from a volume-led to a value-led market, supported by premiumisation across price segments, rising aspirational consumption and growing preference for branded, better-quality offerings, contributing to improved realisations and stronger profitability potential
- Structural long-term demand support from favourable demographics, low per capita consumption, an expanding legal-drinking-age population, rising disposable incomes and increasing global acceptance of Indian spirits
- Premium and super-premium segments continue to outpace broader industry growth, reflecting a structural shift from volume-led to value-led consumption
- Input cost volatility and supply-chain pressures - key inputs such as Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA), glass, grains and packaging materials remain vulnerable to inflationary trends, agricultural variability and supply disruptions, potentially necessitating calibrated pricing actions
- Regulatory and taxation complexity from the state-level regulatory framework affecting pricing, distribution, licensing and route-to-market execution
- Illicit and unorganised market competition creates pricing distortions and can dilute consumer trust in formal categories
- ABD Maestro: two strategically located manufacturing facilities in the pipeline to support efficient small-batch premium production
- Travel Retail: 4 travel retail locations and presence in 4 countries currently, with more locations in the pipeline
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: ABD delivered record FY26 profits driven by premium mix shift and backward integration, with FY27 guidance centered on sustaining margins despite inflationary pressures and scaling ABD Maestro and ICONiQ White to drive mid-teens revenue growth and 300bps EBITDA margin expansion by FY28.

Current backward-integration capex programme (Phase I and Phase II) expected to enhance EBITDA margins by approximately 300 basis points by FY28.
Way-forward (FY28) target for Prestige & Above (P&A) salience to increase to 50% of volumes, from 47.2% in FY26.
Way-forward (FY28) revenue growth guided in the mid-teens, versus 11.5% in FY26.
Way-forward (FY28) target of Gross Margin around 48%, versus 45.6% in FY26.

wtt.summary: 44% guidance hit (17 chains); 1/12 projects on-time; 5 expired; 21% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Confident after seventh consecutive profitable quarter and record FY26; management candid about near-term Q1/Q2 margin pressure from the West Asia war and about OC Blue/SRB7 underperformance, with an ambitious 3-year vision from the incoming MD.

meta.thesis: ABD delivered record FY26 profits driven by premium mix shift and backward integration, with FY27 guidance centered on sustaining margins despite inflationary pressures and scaling ABD Maestro and ICONiQ White to drive mid-teens revenue growth and 300bps EBITDA margin expansion by FY28.
